metadata.title: Marginis, the library of formal marginalia associated with the Journal of Logic and Analysis.

nodes.statement: The Bernoulli measure $\mu_{p}$ is defined by the stipulation that for each $n\in\omega=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$, \[ \mu_p(\{X: X(n)=1\})=p \text{ and } \] \[ \mu_p(\{X:X(n)=0\})=1-p \] and $X(0),X(1),X(2),\ldots$ are mutually independent random variables.
nodes.label: bernoulli

nodes.statement: A $\mu_p$-ML-randomness test is a sequence $\{U^p_n\}_n$ that is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1(p)$ with $\mu(U^p_n)\le 2^{-n}$, where $2^{-n}$ may be replaced by any computable function that goes to zero effectively. A $\mu_p$-ML-randomness test is \emph{Hippocratic} if there is a $\Sigma^0_1$ class $S\subseteq 2^\omega\times\omega$ such that $S=\{(X,n):X\in U_n^p\}$. Thus, $U_n=U_n^p$ does not depend on $p$ and is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$. If $X$ passes all $\mu_p$-randomness tests then $X$ is \emph{$\mu_p$-random}. If $X$ passes all Hippocratic tests then $X$ is \emph{Hippocrates $\mu$-random}.
nodes.label: MLR

nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $Y=\{Y_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ of independent Bernoulli($p$) random variables, with the sample average \[ \overline Y_n := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} Y_i. \] Let $N(b)=2^{3b-1}$ and let \[ U_d=\bigcup_{b\ge d}\{Y: |\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|\ge 2^{-b}\}. \] Then $U_d$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1(p)$, and $\mu_p(U_d)\le 2^{-d}$, i.e., $\{U_d\}_{d\in\omega}$ is a $\mu_p$-ML-test.
nodes.label: is_test

nodes.statement: The fact that $U_d$ is $\Sigma^0_1(p)$ is immediate, so we prove the bound on its $\mu_p$-measure. We have \[ \mathbb{E}(\overline Y_n) = p \text{ and }\sigma^2(\overline Y_n) = \sigma^2/n \] where $\sigma^2=p(1-p)\le 1/4$ is the variance of $Y_0$ and $\sigma^2(\overline Y_n)$ denotes the variance of $\overline Y_n$. Thus $\sigma\le 1/2$, and \[ \mathbb{P}\left\{|\overline Y_n-p|\ge k\cdot\sigma(\overline Y_n)\right\} \le 1/k^2, \] so \[ \mathbb{P}\left\{|\overline Y_n-p|\ge \frac{k}{2\sqrt{n}}\right\} \le \mathbb{P}\left\{|\overline Y_n-p|\ge \frac{k\cdot\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}\right\} \le 1/k^2 =: 2^{-(b+1)}. \] Now, we claim that $2^{-b}\ge\frac{k}{2\sqrt{n}}$ by taking $n$ large enough as a function of $b$: \[ n\ge k^2 4^{b-1}=2^{b+1}4^{b-1}=2^{3b-1}. \] Thus, if $n\ge N(b):=2^{3b-1}$, \[ \mathbb{P}\left\{|\overline Y_n-p|\ge 2^{-b}\right\} \le 2^{-(b+1)} \] so \[ \mathbb{P}\left\{\exists b\ge d\,\,|\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|\ge 2^{-b}\right\} \le \sum_{b\ge d} 2^{-(b+1)}=2^{-d}. \]
If $Y$ is $\mu_p$-ML-random then $Y$ Turing computes $p$.
nodes.label: random_computes

nodes.statement: We may assume $p$ is not computable, else there is nothing to prove; in particular we may assume $p$ is not a dyadic rational. Let $\{U_d\}_{d\in\omega}$ be as in \Cref{is_test}. Since $Y$ is $\mu_p$-random, $Y\not\in\cap_d U_d$, so fix $d$ with $Y\not\in U_d$. Then for all $b\ge d$, we have \[ |\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|< 2^{-b} \tag{*} \] where $N(b)=2^{3b-1}$. If the real number $p$ is represented as a member of $2^\omega$ via \[ p = \sum_{n\in\omega} p_n 2^{-n-1} = .p_0 p_1 p_2\cdots \] in binary notation, then we have to define a Turing functional $\Psi_d$ such that $p_n=\Psi_d^Y(n)$. We pick $b\ge n+1$ such that $\overline Y_{N(b)}=.y_0\cdots y_n\cdots$ is not of either of the forms \[ .y_0\,\cdots \,y_{n} \,1^{b-(n+1)} \cdots \] \[ .y_0\,\cdots \,y_{n} \,0^{b-(n+1)} \cdots \] where as usual $1^k$ denotes a string of $k$ ones. Since $p$ is not a dyadic rational, such a $b$ exists. Then by (*) it must be that the bits $y_0\,\cdots\,y_{n}$ are the first $n+1$ bits of $p$. In particular, $y_n=p_n$. So we let $\Psi_d^Y(n)=y_n$.
There is a Hippocratic $\mu_p$-test such that if $Y$ passes this test then $Y$ computes an accumulation point $q$ of the sequence of sample averages \[ \{\overline Y_n\}_{n\in\omega}. \]
nodes.label: accumulate

nodes.statement: The point is that the usual proof that each convergent sequence is Cauchy gives a $\Sigma^0_1$ class that has small $\mu_p$-measure for all $p$ simultaneously. Namely, let \[ V_d:=\{Y: \exists a,b\ge d\,\,|\overline Y_{N(a)}-\overline Y_{N(b)}|\ge 2^{-a}+ 2^{-b}\}. \] Then $\{V_d\}_{d\in\omega}$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$. Recall from \Cref{is_test} that we defined \[ U^{p}_d=\{Y:\exists b\ge d\,\, |\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|\ge 2^{-b}\}. \] If there is a $p$ such that $|\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|<2^{-b}$ for all $b\ge d$, then \[ |\overline Y_{N(a)}-\overline Y_{N(b)}|\le |\overline Y_{N(a)}-p|+|p-\overline Y_{N(b)}|< 2^{-a}+2^{-b} \] for all $a,b\ge d$; thus we have \[ V_d\subseteq \cap_{p} U^{p}_d \] and therefore \[ \mu_p(V_d)\le\mu_p(U^{p}_d)\le 2^{-d} \] for all $p$. Thus if $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y\not\in V_d$ for some $d$. We next note that for any numbers $c> b$, \[ |\overline Y_{N(b)} - \overline Y_{N(c)}| < 2^{-b}+2^{-c} < 2^{-(b-1)}, \] so $\{\overline Y_{N(c)}\}_{c\ge d}$ will remain within $2^{-(b-1)}$ of $\overline Y_{N(b)}$ for all $c>b$. That is, $\{\overline Y_{N(n)}\}_{n\ge d}$ is a Cauchy sequence (for each $b$ there is an $N(b)$ such that for all $n,m\ge N(b)$, $|\overline Y_n-\overline Y_m|\le 2^{-b}$) hence $q:=\lim_n \overline Y_{N(n)}$ exists. Write $q=.q_0q_1q_2\cdots$. Then \[ |\overline Y_{N(b)}-q| < 2^{-(b-1)}, \text{ so } \] \[ |\overline Y_{N(b+1)}-q| < 2^{-b}; \] if we define $\Theta_d$ as $\Psi_d$ in \Cref{random_computes} except with $N(\cdot)$ replaced by $N(\cdot+1)$, then \[ q_n = \Theta_d^Y(n). \] and so $Y$ computes $q$ using the Turing reduction $\Theta_d$.
If $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y$ satisfies the Strong Law of Large Numbers for $p$.
nodes.label: satisfy_LLN

nodes.statement: Let $q_1$, $q_2$ be rational numbers with $q_1<p<q_2$. Let \[ W_N:=\{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\le q_1\}\cup\{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\ge q_2\} \] Then $\{W_N\}_{N\in\omega}$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$, and $\mu_p W_N\rightarrow 0$ effectively: \[\mu_p \{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\le q_1\} \le \frac{3}{2(p-q_1)^4(N-1)}\] Thus if $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y\not\in\cap_n W_n$, i.e., $\overline Y_n$ is eventually always in the interval $(q_1,q_2)$.
If $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y$ Turing computes $p$.
nodes.label: Hippo_compute

nodes.statement: By \Cref{accumulate}, $Y$ computes the limit of a subsequence $\{\overline Y_{N(b)}\}_{b\in\omega}$. By \Cref{satisfy_LLN}, this limit must be $p$.
For all $p$, if there is a Hippocratic $\mu_p$-test $\{U_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ such that $\{X:X\not\ge_T p\}\subseteq\cap_n U_n$, then $p$ is computable.
nodes.label: not_compute_test

nodes.statement: Let $\{U_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ be such a test. By standard computability theoretic basis theorems, the complement $U_1^c$ has a low member $X_1$ and a hyperimmune-free member $X_2$. By assumption $X_1\ge_T p$ and $X_2\ge_T p$, so $p$ is both low and hyperimmune-free, hence by another basic result of computability theory \cite{Soare}, $p$ is computable.
There is no universal Hippocratic $\mu_p$-test, unless $p$ is computable.
nodes.label: noUniv

nodes.statement: If there is such a test then by \Cref{Hippo_compute} there is a test $\{U_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ as in the hypothesis of \Cref{not_compute_test}, whence $p$ is computable.
Let $k\in\mathbb N$. An automorphisms of $\mathbb Z/ k\mathbb Z$ is a bijection $f$ that preserves addition: \[ f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) \]
nodes.label: def:auto

nodes.statement: The additive structure $\mathbb Z/ k\mathbb Z$ is rigid if it has no nontrivial automorphisms.
nodes.label: def:rigid

nodes.statement: The additive structure $\mathbb Z/ 2\mathbb Z$ is rigid.
nodes.label: thm:rigid
